For our client, an international boutique trust company in Amsterdam we are looking for a Senior Accountant/ financial account manager.

Our client is a highly regarded provider of trust and corporate services for private clients, entrepreneurs, and family-owned businesses.

Our client operates as an international trust boutique with offices in key locations worldwide

Tasks
Job description

You will work in an international and dynamic environment for both corporate and private clients. The companies we manage are mainly Dutch, but some are also located in other jurisdictions. Besides corporate structures, we also manage and handle estate planning structures.

As a senior financial account manager, you will be handling and managing statutory bookkeeping, accounting, and tax compliance as well as assisting in audits for various client companies, as well as other tasks such as transactions, changes, setup and restructuring, working closely with the legal account manager.

An important task of every member of the team is to understand the business of our clients and its full scope. Our clients appreciate a personal approach, high involvement, and dedication. Furthermore, you will also be involved in client acceptance for new clients, setting up new structures, and transaction monitoring.

Requirements
Work experience

At least 5 years of work experience in financial services and/or the financial sector (preferably with a trust office).

Knowledge of IFRS is an asset.

Personal skills

We are looking for a stress-resistant team player with a can-do mentality. Someone, who has excellent organizational skills, an international mindset, and a hands-on approach, is accurate, flexible, and responsible with a demonstrated ability to adapt positively to change.

The candidate should have an excellent command of English and Dutch languages both written and spoken.

Benefits

The Analytical Center of Excellence (ACE) organization is looking for a 
Junior Analytical Technician 
(full shift) in the Chemicals lab located in Terneuzen, The Netherlands.
 

The Chemicals lab in is one of the Manufacturing Production Quality (MPQ) labs that performs analysis of plant-samples in Terneuzen. Servings multiple production plants such as polyurethanes and polyglycols results in the need for a 24/7 service and a full-shift roster to perform the analysis of all plant samples.
 

Responsibilities
 
 

• Ensure service requests are accurately run, and the data returned as per sample plan. 

• Analytical equipment operations and troubleshooting as per procedures. 

• Provide input of quality data into LIMS, document and communicate results. 

• Perform calibration and first line-maintenance of analytical equipment. Document/administrate these maintenance activities. Communicate maintenance work when required. 

• Apply Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S), Analytical Work Process and Operating Discipline/Quality System procedures and practices as well as cGMP/pharma standards. 

• Participating in and completing of laboratory training and corporate required trainings. 

• Co-operate and communicate with co-workers and clients to maintain workflow and instrumental information, and to share and leverage problem solving and prevention expertise. 

• Contribute to value creation by continuous improvement of procedures in the analytical work processes and related tools and performance metrics. 

• Promote a well-organized, responsive, efficient workplace and work well both as a team member and independently. 

Qualifications
 
 

• MBO-4 laboratory degree or similar (bachelors degree preferred). 

• Fluent in Dutch and English. 

• Experience in an industrial laboratory (analytical) 

• Able to work in full shift (24/7 roster): morning, afternoon and night shifts.  

 
 

Preferred qualifications
 
 

• GMP/pharma experience. 

• Experience in operation, calibration, maintenance and troubleshooting of analytical equipment. 

• Knowledge of quality data systems like LIMS, OpenLab, etc. 

• Good lab techniques, methodical record keeping, and the ability to work both independently and with co-workers. 

• Excellent human relations, organizational and communication skills are necessary to communicate with team members, partners and outside customers. 

• Exhibit confidence in confirming validity of methods and data. 

• Able to handle multiple tasks and work under pressure.

During this 9-day course, participants work in teams within a simulated Learning Factory, where they build, analyse and optimise manufacturing lines in a collaborative and competitive setting. 
In addition to the simulation-based programme, participants visit real factories, engage with industry experts and expand their professional network. The course offers a structured and experiential way to explore manufacturing improvement methods and their application in practice.
